title: Affine componentwise normalization and split-node conductor algebra
statement: Let $T$ be a reduced Noetherian commutative ring (Noetherian means every ideal is finitely generated), with minimal primes $\mathfrak p_1,\ldots,\mathfrak p_t$, and put $F_i=\operatorname{Frac}(T/\mathfrak p_i)$. For each $i$ let $\overline T_i$ be the integral closure of $T/\mathfrak p_i$ in $F_i$ [def-weil-pbc-integral-closure]. Then the componentwise normalization [def-weil-pbc-reduced-normalization] of $\operatorname{Spec}T$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum] is canonically $\operatorname{Spec}(\prod_i\overline T_i)$, with structural map induced by $t\mapsto(t\bmod\mathfrak p_i)_i$, and $\prod_i\overline T_i$ is the integral closure of $T$ in $\prod_iF_i$. These descriptions commute with restriction to every principal open. For a normal domain $T$ (an integral domain integrally closed in its fraction field), this normalization map is the identity. In particular, let $R$ be a field or a discrete valuation ring [def-sc-discrete-valuation-ring], $Q=R[u,v]/(uv)$ [def-weil-polynomial-ring], and $E=R[u]\times R[v]$. The map $Q\to E$, $u\mapsto(u,0)$, $v\mapsto(0,v)$, identifies $Q$ with $\{(f,g):f(0)=g(0)\}$ and identifies $E$ with its normalization algebra. It is finite, with $E=Q[e]$ for $e=(1,0)$. The conductor, defined as $I=\{a\in Q:aE\subseteq Q\}$, is $I=(u,v)=uR[u]\times vR[v]$, and $IE=I$, $Q/I=R$, $E/IE=R\times R$. The canonical map $Q\to E\times_{R\times R}R$ is an isomorphism, where $R\to R\times R$ is diagonal. The two branches $\operatorname{Spec}R[u]$, $\operatorname{Spec}R[v]$ and their origins are smooth over $R$ [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]. The empty component product uses the zero ring.

proof.text: Put $X=\operatorname{Spec}T$. It is locally Noetherian, its single affine chart having Noetherian ring $T$ [pqf-def-locnoeth]; by the remark there every quasi-compact open $V\subseteq X$ is locally Noetherian, hence a Noetherian scheme, and so has finitely many irreducible components by [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-finitely-many-components]. By [lem-weil-pbc-spec-irreducible-components-minimal-primes] the generic points of the components of $X$ are its minimal primes $\mathfrak p_1,\ldots,\mathfrak p_t$ (finitely many by the case $V=X$). The residue field at $\mathfrak p_i$ is $T_{\mathfrak p_i}/\mathfrak p_iT_{\mathfrak p_i}=\operatorname{Frac}(T/\mathfrak p_i)=F_i$, with $T$ acting by germs and residues, i.e. through $t\mapsto t\bmod\mathfrak p_i$. Apply [lem-sfb-normalization-generic-residue-affine-charts] to the scheme $X$ and the affine open $U=X$: there $C_X=\prod_iF_i$, $D_X$ is the integral closure of $T$ in $\prod_iF_i$, and $X^\nu\simeq\operatorname{Spec}D_X$ over $X$, the normalization map being induced by $T\to D_X$, $t\mapsto(t\bmod\mathfrak p_i)_i$. Step 2 computes $D_X=\prod_i\overline T_i$. If $T=0$ then $X$ is empty, $t=0$, and the node's empty case gives the zero ring.

For $x=(x_i)\in\prod_iF_i$, a monic equation over $T$ projects to a monic equation over each $T/\mathfrak p_i$. Conversely, if every $x_i\in\overline T_i$, choose a monic $f_i\in(T/\mathfrak p_i)[Z]$ annihilating $x_i$ and lift its coefficients to a monic $g_i\in T[Z]$. The monic polynomial $\prod_i g_i$ annihilates $x$: at coordinate $i$ its factor $g_i(x_i)$ vanishes. Thus the integral closure of $T$ in $\prod_iF_i$ is exactly $\prod_i\overline T_i$, by [def-weil-pbc-integral-closure]. For no factors the ambient ring is zero and its sole element is annihilated by $Z$. With step 1 this gives $X^\nu\simeq\operatorname{Spec}(\prod_i\overline T_i)$, with structural homomorphism $t\mapsto(t\bmod\mathfrak p_i)_i$.

Let $s\in T$ and $W=D(s)=\operatorname{Spec}T_s$. By the compatibility clause of [lem-sfb-normalization-generic-residue-affine-charts], the generic points of $W$ are the $\mathfrak p_i$ with $s
otin\mathfrak p_i$, with unchanged residue fields, so $C_W=\prod_{s
otin\mathfrak p_i}F_i=(\prod_iF_i)_s$: a factor with $s\in\mathfrak p_i$, where $s$ acts as $0$, localizes to zero, and on the others $s$ is already a unit. The node gives $
u^{-1}(W)\simeq\operatorname{Spec}D_W$, and the restriction $D_X	o D_W$ of $
u_*\mathcal O_{X^
u}$ is the projection $C_X	o C_W$. By [lem-weil-pbc-integral-closure-commutes-localization] for $T	o\prod_iF_i$ and the powers of $s$, the integral closure $D_W$ of $T_s$ in $(\prod_iF_i)_s$ is the image of $(D_X)_s=\prod_{s
otin\mathfrak p_i}(\overline T_i)_s$, and restriction sends $b$ to $b/1$. The same node for $T/\mathfrak p_i	o F_i$ identifies $(\overline T_i)_s$ with the integral closure of $(T/\mathfrak p_i)_s=T_s/\mathfrak p_iT_s$ in $F_i$. The minimal primes of the reduced Noetherian ring $T_s$ are the $\mathfrak p_iT_s$ with $s
otin\mathfrak p_i$, so this is the description of steps 1--2 for $T_s$, with the same structural homomorphisms. If $T$ is a normal domain, its only minimal prime is $(0)$, $F_1=\operatorname{Frac}T$, and $\overline T_1=T$ by the definition of normal domain. The structural map is therefore the identity under the canonical identification.

proof.text: Now let $R$ be a field or DVR. The homomorphism $R[u,v]\to R[u]\times R[v]$ sends $h$ to $(h(u,0),h(0,v))$. Its kernel is $(uv)$: expand $h$ in monomials; vanishing of both evaluations means every surviving monomial has both exponents positive and is divisible by $uv$. Its image is exactly the pairs with equal constant coefficients, since $(f,g)$ with $f(0)=g(0)=c$ is the image of $f(u)+g(v)-c$. This proves the claimed identification of $Q$ as a subring of $E$, with the stipulated images of $u,v$.

source.place: Tag 0CDD (lemma-etale-local-at-worst-nodal), split chart; agent polynomial calculation.

proof.text: In $E$ put $e=(1,0)$. For $b=(f,g)$, let $d=f(0)-g(0)\in R$ and $q=(f-d,g)\in Q$. Then $b=q+de$. Thus $E=Q+Qe=Q[e]$, with $1,e$ generating $E$ as a $Q$-module; this proves finiteness directly. Also $e^2=e$, and $b=q+de$ satisfies the monic equation $(Z-q)^2-d(Z-q)=0$ over $Q$. Consequently every element of $E$ is integral over $Q$, without an appeal to a finite-module integrality theorem.

source.place: Tag 0CDD (lemma-etale-local-at-worst-nodal), split chart; agent idempotent and monic-polynomial calculation.

proof.text: Both fields and DVRs are principal ideal domains, so [lem-weil-pbc-pid-noetherian-normal] makes $R$ a normal domain. By [lem-weil-pbc-polynomial-ring-normal-domain], $R[u]$ and $R[v]$ are normal domains. The injection $Q\subset E$ shows $Q$ is reduced. Its minimal primes are $(v)$ and $(u)$: their quotients are the two polynomial domains, and every prime contains $u$ or $v$ since $uv=0$; neither of these two primes contains the other. By [lem-weil-pbc-spec-irreducible-components-minimal-primes], the reduced irreducible components are therefore the two affine lines. Each has identity function-field normalization, since its coordinate ring is integrally closed in its fraction field, by [def-sc-normalization]. The definition [def-weil-pbc-reduced-normalization] and [lem-weil-pbc-finite-affine-coproduct-spectrum] now identify the normalization map with $\operatorname{Spec}E\to\operatorname{Spec}Q$ and its structural map from step 4. No excellence or finiteness of an arbitrary normalization is used.

source.place: Tag 0CDV (lemma-normalization-in-terms-of-components); algebra.tex Tags 00GZ (lemma-PID-normal), 030A (lemma-polynomial-domain-normal); explicit minimal-prime calculation.

proof.text: For $a=(f,g)\in Q$ write $c=f(0)=g(0)$. If $aE\subseteq Q$, multiplication by $e$ gives $(f,0)\in Q$, so $c=0$. Conversely, if $c=0$, then for every $(h,k)\in E$, both constants of $(fh,gk)$ are zero, hence this product is in $Q$. Therefore $I=uR[u]\times vR[v]$. It equals $(u,v)$ as an ideal of $Q$: write $(uf,vg)=u(f,f(0))+v(g(0),g)$, with both coefficient pairs in $Q$. The displayed product ideal is already an ideal of $E$, so $IE=I$. Evaluation at the origins now gives $Q/I=R$ and $E/IE=R\times R$; the induced map is the diagonal.

source.place: Tag 0CDD (lemma-etale-local-at-worst-nodal), split chart; agent conductor and quotient calculation.

proof.text: An element of $E\times_{R\times R}R$ is a pair $((f,g),r)$ with $f(0)=r=g(0)$. Thus $(f,g)\in Q$, and the inverse of the canonical map sends $((f,g),r)$ to the class of $f(u)+g(v)-r$ in $Q$. Step 4 shows the composites are identities: evaluation recovers $(f,g)$, and every class in $Q$ is determined by its two evaluations. These maps preserve sums, products and constants, as can be checked in $E$ through the injective map of step 4. This proves the canonical ring isomorphism.

source.place: Tag 0CDD (lemma-etale-local-at-worst-nodal), split chart; agent fibre-product calculation.

proof.text: The two branches are $\mathbf A^1_{\operatorname{Spec}R}$ and their origins, with their induced reduced structures, are $\operatorname{Spec}R=\mathbf A^0_{\operatorname{Spec}R}$, by [def-sbc-affine-space]. Apply [sbc-lem-affine-space-smooth] with $n=1$ and $n=0$, respectively. Hence all four structural morphisms to $\operatorname{Spec}R$ are smooth, as claimed.
